title: What you see can change what you hear
body: In the McGurk effect, first described in 1976, a video shows a face mouthing ‘ga’ while the soundtrack plays ‘ba’, and many people hear a third sound, ‘da’. Your brain combines lip movements with sound to decode speech, and when the two conflict it settles on a compromise. The illusion often persists even when you know exactly what is going on, but close your eyes and the true sound returns.
